guardrails.rule: A controlled B stage never becomes sellable. A participant A branch remains closed unless an exact Grade-A fulfilment record later authorizes its own route and packet family.

retainedBStage.stageKind: The confidentiality restriction follows the qualifying disposition and is implemented by DPS and other criminal-justice custodians without a petition.
retainedBStage.participantFiles: Nothing. This is the agency-controlled confidentiality stage.

selector.match: A qualifying non-conviction disposition under AS 12.62.160(b)(8), without a claimed record defect or participant backstop request.

productOutcome.description: Explain the confidentiality rule and how to verify the record; do not produce a participant filing.

selector.match: The qualifying record remains inaccurate, incomplete, publicly disseminated, or lacks the disposition that makes it confidential.
selector.exclude: Mistaken-identity and false-accusation sealing must use the existing AS 12.62.180 route; a final adverse agency decision requires the separate review handoff.

participantABranch.instrument: DPS-CRI-103 Request to Correct Criminal Justice Information and a Request for Final Administrative Decision after denial.

documentIdentities.title: Request to Correct Criminal Justice Information in Alaska Public Safety Information Network

relatedParticipantMechanisms.documentTitle: Request to Seal Criminal Justice Information
relatedParticipantMechanisms.routing: Use this existing route for mistaken identity or false accusation; do not send it through the new correction identity.

participantABranch.destination: Alaska Department of Public Safety, Criminal Records and Identification Bureau/Quality Assurance Unit; DPS may forward the request to the contributing agency.
participantABranch.trigger: A non-conviction entry is inaccurate, incomplete, lacks the disposition that makes it confidential, or remains publicly disseminated.
participantABranch.deadline: No deadline for the initial correction request. A request for the commissioner's final administrative decision is due within 30 days after the repository's written denial.
participantABranch.requiredComponents: Identity and contact information; each disputed record item; requested correction; case or arrest identifiers; signed attestation; supporting disposition; and proof of identity.
participantABranch.serviceOrNotice: No adversarial service. DPS decides or forwards the request and must give written notice of denial and review rights.
participantABranch.feeOrWaiver: No correction filing fee is stated. A separate record-copy fee may apply.
participantABranch.selfHelpStop: Stop after a final administrative denial, when identity or false-accusation facts are disputed, or when judicial review or damages are sought.

selector.b: qualifying disposition without a participant defect claim
selector.a: record defect plus participant correction request

scopeNotes: The assignment's NO_EXISTING_WORK result means no form-level match was attempted; it is not a claim that no related route exists.
The new identity is bounded to a non-conviction confidentiality defect and the DPS correction or agency-review process.
Mistaken-identity or false-accusation sealing continues to use obligation:track-pathway:AK:ak-mistaken-identity:sealing-for-mistaken-identity-or-false-accusation-as-12-62-180 and DPS-SEAL-REQ-2-04.

The committed decision-only ak-correct-record route is related evidence, not an approved track/runtime identity. Future integration must reconcile it without collapsing the selectors or output strategies.
A final adverse agency decision hands off to judicial review; it is not part of this agency-application output.

records.publicLabel: Checking whether the one-time cannabis clearing already covered your case

retainedBStage.stageKind: DPSCS was required to purge qualifying cannabis-possession-only cases by July 1, 2024.
retainedBStage.participantFiles: Nothing. This is the one-time DPSCS purge stage.

selector.match: A qualifying cannabis-possession-only record being checked for the one-time section 10-112 purge.

productOutcome.description: Explain purge status and escalation paths without producing a participant filing.

selector.match: A participant-filed section 10-105 matter within the md_10105_favorable track and adult-non-conviction pathway.
selector.scopeWarning: This selector does not cover every cannabis conviction and does not identify the DPSCS correction submission.

participantABranch.instrument: CC-DC-CR-072A Petition for Expungement under section 10-105; DPSCS/CJIS record-correction request for a missed section 10-112 purge.
participantABranch.destination: The court of disposition for the petition; DPSCS CJIS/Central Repository for correction.
participantABranch.trigger: The cannabis-possession-only case was not removed by the July 1, 2024 purge, is independently eligible under section 10-105, or remains on the state record.
participantABranch.deadline: The agency purge was due July 1, 2024. A section 10-105 petition follows its disposition-specific waiting rules; the committed worklist records no separate filing deadline. Correction is requested after discovery.
participantABranch.requiredComponents: Case number, charge and disposition, identity information, CC-DC-CR-072A and any waiver or release, plus a copy of the record showing the uncorrected entry.
participantABranch.serviceOrNotice: The clerk gives statutory notice to the State's Attorney and agencies. Administrative correction is directed to DPSCS.
participantABranch.feeOrWaiver: No court filing fee for the expungement petition; a record-copy fee may apply.
participantABranch.selfHelpStop: Stop for mixed charges, disputed eligibility, State objection, or DPSCS refusal requiring court action.

stopReport.reason: The generated match confirms CC-DC-CR-072A only. It does not bind the DPSCS correction request, and the committed cannabis-specific route uses CC-DC-CR-072D for cannabis charges or convictions. The full REUSE_AS_IS crosswalk is therefore not confirmed.
stopReport.requiredResolution: Define the eligible case scope, identify the DPSCS correction instrument, and resolve the 072A versus 072D route boundary.

records.publicLabel: Clearing fingerprints and an arrest card when you were never charged

retainedBStage.stageKind: The arresting or reporting agency and MSP perform the statutory destruction or correction.
retainedBStage.participantFiles: Nothing when the statutory ministerial destruction occurs as required.

selector.match: The person was arrested and released without charge, and no residual-record or reporting defect is asserted.

productOutcome.description: Explain the ministerial destruction rule and verification steps.

selector.match: No charge was filed or prosecution was declined, and arrest data remains or is reported inaccurately.
selector.exclude: Acquittal or dismissal after charge belongs to the separate mi_arrest_acquittal_dismissal selector even if both routes use MC 235.

participantABranch.filingActor: The person whose arrest record remains.
participantABranch.instrument: Written correction or deletion request to the reporting agency and MSP; MC 235 or other judicial enforcement filing when a court order is required.
participantABranch.destination: The arresting or reporting agency and MSP; the appropriate trial or circuit court for judicial enforcement.
participantABranch.trigger: No charge was filed or prosecution was declined, but arrest data remains or is reported inaccurately.
participantABranch.deadline: No short administrative deadline is recorded. Submit after no-charge status is established or the stale entry is discovered.
participantABranch.requiredComponents: Identity and contact information; arrest date and agency; incident or tracking number; proof no charge was filed; copy of the challenged record; and fingerprints if needed.
participantABranch.serviceOrNotice: Submit to the contributor and MSP. A court filing must serve the responsible custodian or prosecutor as required.
participantABranch.feeOrWaiver: No fee for a correction request. Record, fingerprint, or civil-action costs may apply; court fee waivers are available.
participantABranch.selfHelpStop: Stop if no-charge status or identity is disputed, the agency refuses correction, or civil enforcement becomes contested.

selector.b: never charged with no asserted residual record
selector.a: never charged plus residual or inaccurate arrest data

scopeNotes: The runtime needs a reviewed no-charge fact; a conviction answer must not be used as a proxy.
MC 235 and the named packet family may be shared with the separate acquittal or dismissal route, but the route selectors must remain distinct.
This record identifies the branch. It does not create a packet, acquire the MC 235 source, map fields, or authorize launch.

retainedBStage.stageKind: UCS and DCJS must automatically seal eligible convictions on a phased basis within the implementation window.
retainedBStage.participantFiles: Nothing for ordinary automatic sealing under CPL 160.57.

selector.match: The ny_clean_slate_convictions track and automatic-clean-slate-sealing-under-cpl-160-57 pathway, before a missed-record review or separately eligible court petition is asserted.

participantABranch.bindingScope: The generated match reaches only the separately eligible CPL 160.59 court-filing component. It does not bind the full assigned participant instrument.

selector.match: The person independently satisfies the CPL 160.59 ten-year and eligibility rules and elects discretionary sealing by petition.
selector.exclude: A record that merely remains unsealed during the CPL 160.57 implementation window; UCS manual review and DCJS data correction require separate process treatment.

participantABranch.instrument: For the crosswalked scope, the existing CPL 160.59 sealing application and its committed companion forms.

documentIdentities.title: CPL 160.59 Notice of Motion and Affidavit in Support of Sealing

participantABranch.destination: The superior criminal court for the CPL 160.59 application; file in the court of conviction and serve the county district attorney.
participantABranch.trigger: The person independently qualifies for discretionary conviction sealing under CPL 160.59.
participantABranch.deadline: No separate filing deadline is recorded. The statutory waiting rule is at least ten years from sentencing or release, whichever is later, subject to extensions for later incarceration.
participantABranch.requiredComponents: CPL-160.59-APPLICATION; a Certificate of Disposition for each case; the pro se packet; sworn prior-application statement; rehabilitation material; service proof; and post-order verification.
participantABranch.serviceOrNotice: Serve the county district attorney with proof. The district attorney may oppose, and the court may hold a hearing.
participantABranch.feeOrWaiver: Court filing charges and waivers follow UCS rules.
participantABranch.selfHelpStop: Stop for disputed time calculations, pending-charge tolling, registry or offense exclusions, prosecutor opposition, or appeal.

scopeNotes: No committed CPL 160.57 manual-review form ID or specific DCJS challenge form was found.
The proposed crosswalk must not claim that the CPL 160.59 court packet performs UCS manual review or DCJS correction.
REUSE_AS_IS reuses the canonical route identity, not a completed packet implementation.

stopReport.reason: The CPL 160.59 form match covers only the discretionary court petition. The assigned participant instrument also includes CPL 160.57(e) manual review and a DCJS record challenge, and neither action is bound to the existing A route.
stopReport.requiredResolution: Identify and route the manual-review and DCJS challenge processes, then confirm whether they require separate participant_agency_application identities before approving any reuse crosswalk.
